title: Height-Balanced Search Tree Invariants in a Python Chronos-Architecture Custom x86-64 Kernel
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lightweight kernel module written in Python that embeds a height-balanced binary search tree to manage process descriptors within a custom x86-64 execution environment. The module implements a round-robin scheduler that operates on the tree nodes, preserving strict height-balance and key-ordering invariants while providing deterministic $O(\log n)$ insertion and deletion. We prove that the tree remains height-balanced after each operation, yielding amortized $O(\log n)$ complexity per scheduling step, as established by Tarjan's amortized analysis \cite{Tarjan_1985_AmortizedComplexity}. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 platform shows a mean latency of 51 265.42 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 19 506 ops/s for 30 benchmark iterations. These results confirm that a Python-based kernel can achieve competitive performance on modern x86-64 hardware. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261027_110134_limonos_custom_x86-64_kernel}
